title: Six Prompts Under the J-lens
takeaway: Six short prompts, each with J-lens readouts at a few middle layers, show the model's unspoken intermediate assessments: the bridging fact Mars in a two-hop question, the running values 21 and 42 in an arithmetic problem, protein / fluor / green over a raw amino-acid sequence, empty / ERROR / ValueError at a buggy function call, eyes and nose on an ASCII drawing, and prompt / fake / injection inside fabricated search results. In every case the concept tops the readout at middle depth before anything is said, while the final layer has already flipped to the literal next token.
walkthrough:
This item is a live widget, not a static image. Under the header "The J-lens reveals the model's internal thoughts across layers" sit six small panels. Each is one short prompt run through Sonnet 4.5 ([[claude-model-family]]); the prompt-injection panel alone is labeled Opus 4.5.

Each panel prints its prompt with one or two token positions highlighted. Beside it stands a stack of rows, one per sampled layer, labeled L42 through L99. The paper samples 25 evenly spaced layers and reindexes them 0–100, so a layer number reads as a percentage of depth ([[layer-percentage-indexing]]); L50 is halfway through the model. Each row prints the top-ranked token of the [[j-lens-readout]] there — the [[residual-stream]] activation at that layer and position, passed through the [[jacobian-lens]]. A parenthesized number appears when the shown token ranks below first. Clicking any prompt token moves the readout, and a slice-viewer link opens the full grid.

A row is not a next-token prediction. The lens matrix is a Jacobian averaged over a thousand contexts, so a row names what the activation disposes the model to say, now or in some later continuation — a [[verbalizable-representation]].

Three panels catch reasoning intermediates. Multihop Recall runs "The color of the planet fourth from the sun is": at the last token the rows read color (L50), Mars (L71), red (L99) — the bridging entity ([[multihop-benchmark]]) appears in neither prompt nor answer. Mental Arithmetic runs "calc: (4+17)*2+7 =". The sum 4+17 is 21; 21 times 2 is 42; 42 plus 7 is 49. At the equals sign the rows read Math (L58), 21 (L75), 42 (L83), 49 (L99) — the intermediates surface in computation order ([[order-of-operations-benchmark]]). Protein Recognition asks "What is this?" of the first 60 residues of avGFP; five characters in, the lens reads protein (L58), then fluor (L58) and green (L83) — the green fluorescent protein, identified from raw sequence.

Three panels catch silent assessments. Bug detection: at the call avg([]), on an empty list, the rows read empty (L42), ERROR (L54), ValueError (L71) before any output exists. ASCII Face: eyes at an "o" of the drawing, nose and faces at the "^". Prompt injection: inside text glossed "[fabricated news search results inside a tool call]", the rows read prompt (L42), fake (L58), injection (L88) — the silent recognition that section 5 builds into [[alignment-auditing]].

The pattern across all six: the abstract concept occupies the middle depths — the [[workspace-layers]] — while the L99 row has flipped to the imminent output (red, 49, the next sequence letter g), the paper's motor regime ([[motor-layers]]).

terms.definition: The paper's readout technique: for each layer, a corpus-averaged Jacobian composed with the unembedding gives every vocabulary token a score against any residual-stream activation. Every row of every panel is one such readout.
The ranked vocabulary list softmax(W_U norm(J_l h_l)) for one activation. Each panel row shows only its top entry at one (layer, position) point.

terms.term: The J-lens reveals the model's internal thoughts across layers
terms.definition: The widget's own header line, naming what the six panels jointly demonstrate.
The Claude model five of the six prompts are run on; the mid-size tier of the family used throughout the paper.
The larger Claude model used for the prompt-injection panel only, as its panel title notes.
Depth labels on each readout row. The paper samples 25 evenly spaced layers indexed 0–100, so the number is a percentage of depth; the final layer (100) is displayed as L99 in this figure.
Each layer row prints only the single highest-scoring lens token at the highlighted position; the full ranked list is available in the linked slice viewer.
A small number after a row's token when that token is not rank 1 in the readout at that cell.
The position the readout stack is read at, marked in the prompt text. Clicking another prompt token moves the readout there.
Panel running "The color of the planet fourth from the sun is": a two-hop question whose bridging entity (Mars) must be computed but never said.
Top lens tokens at the Multihop panel's final position: the question topic at L50, the unspoken bridging entity at L71, and the answer at L99.
Panel running "calc: (4+17)*2+7 =", an order-of-operations problem in which partial results must be computed before the remaining operations.
Top lens tokens at the equals sign: a task label at L58, then the running values 21 (=4+17) at L75 and 42 (=21×2) at L83, then the final answer 49 at L99.
Panel asking "What is this?" of the raw amino-acid sequence of avGFP, the green fluorescent protein of the jellyfish Aequorea victoria; the model is given only the letter sequence.

Top lens tokens a few characters into the sequence: protein at L58, then fluor (completing to fluorescent) at L58 and green at L83 two positions later — the protein's identity, read off the raw residues.
Panel showing a Python snippet defining avg(xs) = sum(xs)/len(xs) and then calling print(avg([])) — a call that will fail on the empty list.
Top lens tokens at the closing of avg([]): the model has registered the empty argument at L42 and an impending error at L54 and L71, with no output yet produced.
Panel showing a face drawn in ASCII characters inside a box: two "o" eyes, a "^" nose, an underscore mouth.
Top lens tokens on the drawing: eyes at an "o" (L54–L83), and facial (L54), nose (L71), faces (L83) at the "^" — the model has parsed the characters as a face and its parts.

Panel reading the lens inside fabricated news-style search results returned by a tool call; the excerpt ends "… told MIT Tech Review on condition of anonymity." and the readout is taken at the token anonym.

terms.term: [fabricated news search results inside a tool call]
terms.definition: The panel's gloss explaining where its text excerpt comes from: an auditing agent returned invented search results to the model inside a tool response.
Top lens tokens inside the fabricated results, at L42, L58, and L88 respectively: the model has silently classified the content as a prompt-injection attempt.
The per-position vector each layer reads from and writes to; the activation each readout row is computed from.
The article's companion tool, linked from the caption, that opens each of these prompts as a full (position, layer) grid of readouts.

numbers.meaning: The number of prompt panels: three reasoning intermediates (multihop, arithmetic, protein) and three silent assessments (code bug, ASCII face, prompt injection).
The paper's layer convention: 25 evenly spaced residual-stream layers reindexed so a layer number reads as a percentage of depth. This figure displays the final layer (100) as L99.

The sampled depths each panel shows: multihop L50/L71/L99, arithmetic L58/L75/L83/L99, protein L58/L83/L99, bug L42/L54/L71, face L54/L71/L83, injection L42/L58/L88. Middle rows carry the abstract concept; the deepest rows shade into the output.
The operands of the arithmetic prompt (4+17)*2+7, chosen so the bracketed sum must be computed before the multiplication and addition.
4+17, the first intermediate value; it tops the readout at L75, unspoken.
21×2, the second intermediate value; it tops the readout at L83, one sampled layer deeper than 21 — the intermediates surface in computation order.
42+7, the final answer; it tops the readout only at L99, where the lens reflects the imminent output.
The planet's position in the multihop prompt; resolving "the planet fourth from the sun" to Mars is the unspoken first hop, visible at L71.
Roughly the number of amino-acid residues of avGFP shown in the protein panel (the sequence beginning MSKGEELFTG…).
How far into the sequence the readout position sits when protein first tops the lens — after only M, S, K, G, E, per the panel caption.
Each row shows only the readout's highest-ranked token; a parenthesized rank appears when the displayed token is not first.
Highlighted readout positions per panel: one in most panels, two in the protein and face panels.
The pretraining-like corpus each layer's Jacobian is averaged over — the reason a readout names a context-general disposition to verbalize rather than this prompt's next token.
